title: Derived coinduction cancels added evaluation variables
statement:
Let $R\to P\xrightarrow{\psi} A$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings, let $m\geq0$, and choose $g_1,\ldots,g_m\in P$. Set $Q=P[y_1,\ldots,y_m]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], let $\pi:Q\twoheadrightarrow P$ send $y_i$ to $g_i$, and set $\chi=\psi\pi$. For a ring map $T\to B$, write $C_B^T:D(T)\to D(B)$ for derived coinduction [def-trf-derived-coinduction], namely $\operatorname{Hom}_T(B,I)$ for a K-injective representative $I$ with action $(b h)(b')=h(b'b)$. Use ordinary unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. There is an isomorphism of functors $D(R)\to D(A)$
$$C_A^Q(-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q)[m]\ \cong\ C_A^P(-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}P).$$
There is also an isomorphism of functors $D(Q)\to D(P)$
$$C_P^Q(-)\ \cong\ (-\otimes_Q^{\mathbf L}P)[-m].$$
The comparisons may depend on the ordered variables and the chosen $g_i$; no comparison independent of those choices is asserted. No flatness of $P/R$, surjectivity of $\psi$, Noetherianity, or boundedness of the input complex is assumed.

source.place: Tags 0BZH (lemma-compute-for-effective-Cartier-algebraic) and 0BZJ (lemma-well-defined), evaluation quotient and induction on the added polynomial variables.

proof.text:
First work with one variable: $S=T[y]$, $q:S\to T$, $y\mapsto g$, and $z=y-g$. For $f=\sum a_k y^k$ the identity
$$f(y)-f(g)=(y-g)\sum_{k\geq1}a_k\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}y^{k-1-j}g^j$$
shows $\ker q=(z)$; constants show surjectivity. Multiplication by $z$ is injective: if $f\ne0$ and $a_d\ne0$ is its highest nonzero coefficient, the coefficient of $y^{d+1}$ in $zf$ is $a_d$. Thus $S\xrightarrow{z}S\to T\to0$ is exact. The ideal $I=(z)$ is free of rank one via $a\mapsto az$, and the displayed two-term finite free resolution makes $T[0]$ perfect over $S$ by [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. If $S=0$ the maps and claims are the unique zero maps and the same free-module identifications still apply.

source.place: Tag 0BZJ, lemma-well-defined, one-variable evaluation quotient; elementary verification of its kernel and finite free resolution.

proof.text:
For this quotient, [lem-trf-cartier-quotient-derived-dual] gives $D_T=C_T^S(S[0])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_T(I\otimes_S T,T)[-1]$ in $D(T)$. The generator $z$ identifies $I\otimes_S T$ with $T$, so its dual identifies with $T$ by evaluation on $z\otimes1$. Since Step 1 proved perfection, [lem-trf-perfect-algebra-coinduction-tensor] now gives, naturally for every $M\in D(S)$,
$$C_T^S(M)\cong M\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}D_T\cong(M\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}T)[-1].$$
The second isomorphism uses functoriality in the second tensor factor from [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor]. Shifting the second factor by $-1$ shifts its total tensor by $-1$: on a summand $F^a\otimes T^b$ the cochain identification multiplies by $(-1)^a$, which respects the two tensor differentials. All these maps are $T$-linear; the dual comparison is in $D(T)$, and the perfect-algebra comparison retains that same action.

For arbitrary ring maps $S\to T\to B$, [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction] identifies each coinduction as the right adjoint of scalar restriction. The composite of the two restriction functors is restriction along $S\to B$. Hence [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition] supplies a natural isomorphism
$$C_B^S\cong C_B^T C_T^S.$$
Coinduction commutes with shifts: in its defining K-injective model, shifting $I$ shifts $\operatorname{Hom}_T(B,I)$ with the same differential signs and the same action. A shifted K-injective is K-injective, since testing Hom from an acyclic complex reduces to testing its opposite shift. In particular $C_B^T(L[r])\cong C_B^T(L)[r]$. Identity coinduction is the identity, by $\operatorname{Hom}_T(T,I)\cong I$, $h\mapsto h(1)$ [def-trf-derived-coinduction].

source.place: Tag 0C0F, lemma-composition-right-adjoints; Tag 0A71, lemma-RHom-ext, and the K-injective construction in section-trivial.

proof.text:
Put $Q_i=P[y_1,\ldots,y_i]$ and let $q_i:Q_i\to Q_{i-1}$ evaluate $y_i$ at $g_i$. Inductively construct a natural isomorphism
$$C_P^{Q_i}(M)\cong(M\otimes_{Q_i}^{\mathbf L}P)[-i]\quad(M\in D(Q_i)).$$
For $i=0$ use identity coinduction and $M\otimes_P P=M$. For the successor, Step 3 identifies $C_P^{Q_i}$ with $C_P^{Q_{i-1}}C_{Q_{i-1}}^{Q_i}$; apply Step 2 to the latter factor, then the induction hypothesis and shift compatibility. This gives
$$((M\otimes_{Q_i}^{\mathbf L}Q_{i-1})\otimes_{Q_{i-1}}^{\mathbf L}P)[-i].$$
To identify its tensor with $M\otimes_{Q_i}^{\mathbf L}P$, choose a K-flat representative $F$ of $M$. Scalar extension preserves K-flatness by [lem-pc-kflat-extension-of-scalars], and [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] computes both derived extensions on these representatives. The required cochain isomorphism sends $(f\otimes a)\otimes p$ to $f\otimes\pi_{i-1}(a)p$, with inverse $f\otimes p\mapsto(f\otimes1)\otimes p$, where $\pi_{i-1}:Q_{i-1}\to P$ is evaluation. Balancing proves the inverse identities; both maps commute with differentials and with maps of $F$. Resolution independence is included in the cited tensor-functor statement. At $i=m$ this is the second asserted functor isomorphism, including $m=0$.

source.place: Tag 0BZJ, lemma-well-defined, induction on the added variables; K-flat computation of successive scalar extensions.

proof.text:
For $K\in D(R)$ put $M=K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q$. A K-flat representative $F$ of $K$ extends to the K-flat $Q$-complex $F\otimes_R Q$ by [lem-pc-kflat-extension-of-scalars]. The computation rule of [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] identifies
$$(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q)\otimes_Q^{\mathbf L}P\cong K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}P.$$
The cochain maps are $(f\otimes q)\otimes p\mapsto f\otimes\pi(q)p$ and $f\otimes p\mapsto(f\otimes1)\otimes p$, natural in $F$. This uses no flatness of $P/R$. Combine this identification with Step 4 to obtain $C_P^Q(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q)\cong(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}P)[-m]$, naturally in $K$.

source.place: Tag 0BZJ, lemma-well-defined, final tensor substitution, computed without a flatness assumption.

proof.text:
Finally apply Step 3 to $Q\xrightarrow{\pi}P\xrightarrow{\psi}A$ and then apply $C_A^P$ to Step 5. The resulting natural isomorphisms are
$$C_A^Q(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q)[m]\cong C_A^P(C_P^Q(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q))[m]\cong C_A^P((K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}P)[-m])[m]\cong C_A^P(K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}P).$$
The last map uses the shift comparison of Step 3 and cancels the two shifts. This is in $D(A)$ throughout. Choices of the ordered generators provide the trivializations in Step 2 and fix the order of induction; no independence of those choices has been used. Neither the adjunction nor the tensor computations required $\psi$ surjective, bounded input, or Noetherian rings.

source.place: Tag 0BZJ, lemma-well-defined, the displayed composite and shift cancellation.
